rules.explanation: Storing plain text passwords, using weak JWT signing algorithms, or omitting token expiration mechanisms exposes identity servers to total compromise.
rules.do: Hash passwords using robust memory-hard algorithms (e.g., Argon2, bcrypt) and implement stateless JWT access/refresh token rotation with TLS.
rules.dont: Do not store unhashed passwords, encode sensitive PII inside JWT payloads, or rely on weak MD5/SHA1 algorithms.

rules.explanation: Exposing backend endpoints without throughput restrictions allows brute-force attacks and resource exhaustion (Denial of Service).
rules.do: Implement API rate limiting per IP or client token (e.g., Leaky Bucket / Token Bucket algorithms via Redis or Reverse Proxies).
rules.dont: Do not leave authentication, registration, or computational API endpoints unprotected against unbounded request bursts.

rules.rule_name: Asynchronous Task Offloading and Message Queues
rules.explanation: Executing long-running tasks (e.g., video processing, email dispatch) synchronously inside HTTP request cycles causes gateway timeouts and server unresponsiveness.
rules.do: Offload heavy background execution to asynchronous message brokers and task queues (e.g., RabbitMQ, Kafka, Celery).
rules.dont: Do not block HTTP request handler execution threads with heavy I/O or long-running synchronous batch operations.

rules.rule_name: Strict CORS and Input Injection Defense
rules.explanation: Permissive CORS policies (Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *) combined with unsanitized parameters expose backends to Cross-Site Hijacking and SQL/Command Injection.
rules.do: Restrict CORS policies strictly to trusted origins, utilize parameterized ORM queries, and sanitize all headers/inputs.
rules.dont: Do not use wildcard '*' CORS configurations in production or construct SQL queries via raw string concatenation.
